title: Dedicated Autoscale OKRs, Metrics, and Playbook — Q2 Roadmap
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: produce a clear Q2 roadmap that ties 3 concrete OKRs to measurable metrics and a runbook for Dedicated autoscale behavior. Scope covers: policy primitives (min/max pools, burst lanes, fractional reservations), canary and fast-fail strategies, prewarm heuristics, fairshare and priority queues, and the observability/alerts necessary for safe rollouts.

Why now: customers are increasingly sensitive to latency tail events during short bursts and we need a repeatable operating model to avoid costly over-provisioning while preserving SLOs. Current gap: lack of an operational playbook that maps signal -> action for surge events and no standard metric set to correlate cost vs. error/latency regressions across dedicated pools.

Planned deliverables (Q2 slice):
1) OKRs and target metrics:
   - OKR 1 (Reliability): Reduce P99 inference latency tail during 30s burst windows by 20% for dedicated customers classified as "high-throughput". Metrics: P99 latency, warm-pool hit rate, autoscale time-to-capacity.
   - OKR 2 (Economics): Reduce excess committed GPU minutes during non-peak hours by 12% while keeping SLOs stable. Metrics: hourly utilization variance, cost-per-1M tokens, idle GPU minutes per pool.
   - OKR 3 (Operational readiness): Enable automated canary rollback for autoscale policies with <10% manual interventions across all rollouts. Metrics: percent of rollouts with automated rollback, mean time-to-detect anomaly, runbook adherence rate.

2) Playbook & runbooks:
   - Surge detection thresholds and initial containment actions (traffic shaping, shed-low-priority, safe fallback to smaller model variants).
   - Warm pool tuning guidance by workload archetype (chat, batch embeddings, long-context generation).
   - Canary lanes: how to schedule small traffic slices, what telemetry to collect, and gating criteria for progressive ramps.
   - Fast-fail choreography: ordering of fallback (model variant -> region -> degrade mode) and escalation path to SRE & account owners.

3) Metricization and dashboards:
   - Standard metric set to ship: p50/p95/p99 latency; queue length; warm-pool hit rate; autoscale decision latency; GPU utilization (1m/5m); cost per token estimates; rollback count.
   - New composite metric: "Autoscale Inefficiency Index" (stringified definition in attached doc) to help trade off cost vs latency regressions.

4) Experiments & acceptance criteria:
   - Experiment A: aggressive prewarm for 2 high-volume customers in staging -> measure P99 improvement and cost delta. Success = >=15% P99 improvement with <=6% incremental cost.
   - Experiment B: fractional reservations pilot to test 60/40 split for base vs burst lanes on one pool. Success = reduction in idle GPU minutes by 10% without SLO regressions.

Stakeholders and reviewers: product (Maya Chen, Arjun Patel), SRE (Lina Gomez), Runtime Eng (Diego Ramos), Billing (Priya Shah), Solutions Eng (Tom Ellison), Legal for contract-impact review.

Acceptance criteria for "Done":
- OKRs published and approved by GTM lead.
- Playbook document committed in Confluence with runbook checklists and escalation contacts.
- Dashboard mocks implemented in Console staging with required panels.
- Two experiments scheduled and one canary rollout automation PR merged with test coverage.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: mis-tuned prewarm increases committed spend. Mitigation: require cost guardrail and experiment budget; abort conditions defined.
- Risk: rollback automation false positives. Mitigation: staged canaries and human-in-loop during first 2 production rollouts.

Notes about scope boundaries: this ticket focuses on orchestration, playbooks, and metricization. Changes to kernel selection, quantization, or model artifacts are out of scope and will be coordinated via ENG tickets.

Next steps: 1) stakeholder alignment meeting (scheduled 2026-01-12), 2) finalize OKRs (by 2026-01-22), 3) create ENG tickets for telemetry gaps (target 2026-01-29), 4) schedule pilot customers for experiments (target 2026-02-05).
